''Les Carolos'' | founded = {{Start date and years ago|1904|1|1|df=y}} | ground = [[Stade du Pays de Charleroi]] | capacity = 15,000[http://sporting-charleroi.be/club-stade.php/ Het Stade du Pays de Charleroi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100817061428/http://sporting-charleroi.be/club-stade.php/ |date=17 August 2010 }} sporting-charleroi.be (last check 30 March 2018) | owntitle = Chairman | owner = Fabien Debecq{{cite news|title=Fabien Debecq nouveau président du Sporting de Charleroi|url=http://www.rtl.be/sport/football/football-belgique/football-fabien-debecq-nouveau-president-du-sporting-de-charleroi-563097.aspx|access-date=5 October 2015|work=RTL Sport|publisher=RTL Belux S.A.|date=6 September 2012}} | chrtitle = Managing Director | chairman = [[Mehdi Bayat]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = Mario Kohnen | league = {{Belgian football updater|RoyalCharleroiSC}} | season = {{Belgian football updater|RoyalCharleroiSC2}} | position = {{Belgian football updater|RoyalCharleroiSC3}} | current = 2025–26 Royal Charleroi S.C. season | website = {{URL|https://www.sporting-charleroi.be}} | pattern_la1 = _charleroi2425h | pattern_b1 = _charleroi2425h | pattern_ra1 = _charleroi2425h | pattern_sh1 = _charleroi2425h | pattern_so1 = _charleroi2425h | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FFFFFF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = _charleroi2425a | pattern_b2 = _charleroi2425a | pattern_ra2 = _charleroi2425a | pattern_sh2 = _charleroi2425a | pattern_so2 = _charleroi2425a | leftarm2 = 000000 | body2 = 000000 | rightarm2 = 000000 | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 }} '''Royal Charleroi Sporting Club''', often simply known as '''Charleroi''' or '''Sporting Charleroi''', is a Belgian professional [[association football|football]] club based in the city of [[Charleroi]], in the province of [[Hainaut (province)|Hainaut]]. Charleroi plays in the [[Belgian Pro League]]. Their current spell at the highest level in Belgian football started in the [[2012–13 Belgian Pro League|2012–13 season]]. Charleroi was founded in 1904 and they first reached the first division in [[Belgian First Division 1947–48|1947–48]]. Their highest finish was runner-up in the [[Belgian First Division 1968–69|1968–69 season]]. They have also twice reached the [[Belgian Cup]] final, losing in [[1977–78 Belgian First Division|1977–78]] to [[K.S.K. Beveren|Beveren]] and in [[1992–93 Belgian Cup|1992–93]] to [[Standard Liège]]. Sporting Charleroi have a long-standing rivalry with their crosstown rival [[R.O.C. de Charleroi-Marchienne|ROC de Charleroi-Marchienne]], currently playing in the [[Belgian Third Division|third division]]. Charleroi play their home matches at the [[Stade du Pays de Charleroi]], which was refurbished for the [[UEFA Euro 2000]]. The stadium hosted 3 group stage games in the Euro 2000 among which the 1–0 victory of [[England national football team|England]] against [[Germany national football team|Germany]]. Charleroi have been recruiting several French players in recent years, including [[Michaël Ciani]], [[Cyril Théréau]] and [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Bertrand Laquait]]."}}
